ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Embryogenesis is a carefully timed and well-organized process. As a single-celled zygote divides and grows into hundreds and thousands of cells, a process called differentiation occurs wherein certain areas of the embryo become specialized to become different types of tissue. As differentiation continues, the level of specificity increases, and the cell potency decreases until highly specialized unique tissues and organs develop. The figure below shows 12 stages of development of human embryos.A totipotent embryonic cell has the most cell potency. Which of the following is most likely to be totipotent?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Embryogenesis is a carefully timed and well-organized process in which cell potency decreases as differentiation proceeds. Which embryonic stage is most likely to be totipotent?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the stages of human embryonic development by number: 1 is fertilised egg, 2 is 8-cell zygote, followed in order by cell adhesion, 16-cell morula, blastocyst, zona hatching, invades uterine wall, cell mass differentiates (labeling epiblast, hypoblast, trophoblast), bilaminar disc forms, mesoderm forms, mesoderm spreads, amniotic sac grows. Reasoning: The question stem states that as differentiation proceeds, cell potency decreases; totipotency is the highest level of cell potency, so it should appear at the earliest stage, where there has not yet been obvious differentiation or formation of different germ layers/tissue lineages. Among the stages shown in the figure, the early cleavage-stage 8-cell zygote is before cell adhesion, morula, blastocyst, and germ-layer differentiation, and best matches the characteristics of totipotency.
